items.title: 1.4.1 Properties of Cube Roots of Unity (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq (1.4) mein humne unity ke teen cube roots nikaale the: \(1\), \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\) aur \(\frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\). Yeh fractions likhna har dafa thaka dene wala hai. Is sabaq mein hum in roots ki teen khoobiyan (properties) seekhenge, aur ek chhota naam \(\omega\) (omega) denge jis se sawal bohat aasan ho jate hain. Exercise 1.4 ke taqreeban saare sawal inhi properties par chalte hain, is liye inhein dil se samajhiye.
(i) Each complex cube root of unity is square of the other
Yani har complex cube root doosre ka square hai. Agar \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega\) ho, to \(\frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega^{2}\),
aur agar \(\frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega\) ho, to \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega^{2}\) [\(\omega\) ko "omega" parha jata hai]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab doosri line mein pehla root hi dobara likh deti hai: "if \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega\), then \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega^{2}\)". Yeh mumkin nahin, kyun ke ek hi number \(\omega\) bhi ho aur \(\omega^{2}\) bhi, aisa nahin hota. Sahi yeh hai: agar \(\frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega\) to \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega^{2}\). Matlab: jis complex root ko bhi \(\omega\) kahein, doosra \(\omega^{2}\) hoga.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Property (i) sahi kyun hai? Khud square kar ke dekhte hain, \((a + b)^{2}\) ke formula se:
\[\left(\dfrac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)^{2} = \dfrac{1 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i + 3i^{2}}{4}\]
\[= \dfrac{-2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i}{4} = \dfrac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\]
Yahan \(3i^{2} = -3\) ne \(1\) ko \(-2\) bana diya, aur phir 2 se kaat diya. Isi tarah \(\left(\frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\).
Natija: unity ke teen cube roots ko ab aise likhte hain: \(1, \omega, \omega^{2}\). Lambe fractions ki jagah do chhote nishaan!
(ii) The sum of all the three cube roots of unity is zero
Yani teenon cube roots ka jor (sum) zero hai:

blocks.text_alt: 1 plus omega plus omega squared equals 0

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun? Seedha jama kar ke dekhiye: \(1 + \frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} + \frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = 1 + \frac{-2}{2} = 0\). Imaginary hisse \(+\sqrt{3}\,i\) aur \(-\sqrt{3}\,i\) aapas mein khatam ho jate hain.
Doosra tareeqa: \(\omega\) equation \(x^{2} + x + 1 = 0\) ka root hai (1.4 yaad kijiye), is liye \(\omega^{2} + \omega + 1 = 0\).
Sawalon mein yeh property aksar doosri shaklon mein kaam aati hai, inhein yaad kar lein:
\(\omega + \omega^{2} = -1\), \(1 + \omega = -\omega^{2}\), \(1 + \omega^{2} = -\omega\).
Har shakal \(1 + \omega + \omega^{2} = 0\) mein se ek term doosri taraf le jane se bani hai.
(iii) The product of all the three cube roots of unity is unity
Yani teenon cube roots ka zarb (product) 1 hai:

blocks.text_alt: 1 times omega times omega squared equals omega cubed equals 1

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun? \(\omega\) unity ka cube root hai, to definition hi se \(\omega^{3} = 1\). Seedha multiply kar ke bhi dekh sakte hain: \(\omega \cdot \omega^{2} = \frac{(-1)^{2} - (\sqrt{3}\,i)^{2}}{4} = \frac{1 + 3}{4} = 1\).
Is property ka sab se bara faida: kyun ke \(\omega^{3} = 1\), is liye \(\omega\) ki koi bhi bari power chhoti ki ja sakti hai. Power ko 3 se divide karein aur sirf remainder (baqi) rakhein. Socheiye ghari ki suiyan: 12 ke baad phir 1 aata hai. Isi tarah \(\omega\) ki powers bhi har 3 ke baad dobara shuru ho jati hain: \(\omega, \omega^{2}, 1, \omega, \omega^{2}, 1, \dots\)

blocks.caption: ω ki powers har 3 ke baad dohrati hain

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
\(\omega^{28}\) ko chhota karna ho to: \(28 = 3 \times 9 + 1\), is liye \(\omega^{28} = (\omega^{3})^{9}\omega = 1^{9} \cdot \omega = \omega\).
Sawal mein jahan bhi \(1 + \omega\) nazar aaye use \(-\omega^{2}\) se, aur \(\omega + \omega^{2}\) ko \(-1\) se badal dein. Aksar poora sawal do teen lines mein hal ho jata hai.
Khud sochiye: \(\omega^{29}\) kya hoga? (Jawab: \(29 = 3 \times 9 + 2\), to \(\omega^{2}\).)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ek chhota sa sawal (kitab ka nahin, practice ke liye): \((1 + \omega)^{3}\) ki value?
\(1 + \omega = -\omega^{2}\) (property (ii) se).
To \((1 + \omega)^{3} = (-\omega^{2})^{3} = -\omega^{6} = -(\omega^{3})^{2} = -1\).
Dekhiye, lambi multiplication ki zaroorat hi nahin pari.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Unity ke cube roots \(1, \omega, \omega^{2}\) hain; har complex root doosre ka square hai.
2. Jor: \(1 + \omega + \omega^{2} = 0\) (aur is ki shaklein \(\omega + \omega^{2} = -1\), \(1 + \omega = -\omega^{2}\), \(1 + \omega^{2} = -\omega\)).
3. Zarb: \(\omega^{3} = 1\), is liye \(\omega\) ki powers har 3 ke baad dohrati hain; power ko 3 se divide kar ke remainder rakhein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\omega\) ko sirf ek pakka root samajhna: dono complex roots mein se kisi ko bhi \(\omega\) keh sakte hain; doosra phir \(\omega^{2}\) hoga.
2. \(1 + \omega + \omega^{2} = 1\) likh dena, yani jor (sum = 0) aur zarb (product = 1) mein ulajh jana.
3. \(\omega^{n}\) chhota karte waqt \(n\) ko 2 se divide karna; hamesha 3 se divide karein, kyun ke \(\omega^{3} = 1\).
4. \(\omega^{2}\) ko "\(\omega\) ka double" samajhna: yeh \(\omega \times \omega\) hai, \(2\omega\) nahin.
